easy.explanation: The passage begins, “Who is this that cometh from Edom?”
easy.q: From where does the figure come at the beginning of the passage?

easy.explanation: The garments are described as dyed and red, like the garments of one who treads in the winefat.
easy.q: How are the figure’s garments described?

easy.explanation: The figure says, “I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the people there was none with me.”

answers: The blood of the nations was sprinkled upon them
medium.explanation: The figure says that the blood of the people was sprinkled upon the garments and stained the raiment.
medium.q: Why are the figure’s garments red?

answers: A time of judgment against the enemies
A day when the temple would be built
medium.explanation: The figure declares, “For the day of vengeance is in mine heart.”
medium.q: What does “the day of vengeance” mean in this passage?

medium.explanation: The word “glorious” describes the figure as majestic or impressive in appearance.
medium.q: What does “glorious in his apparel” most nearly mean?

answers: The work was accomplished by his own power
The figure did not know how to fight
challenge.explanation: The passage says there was none to help or uphold him, so his own arm brought salvation.
challenge.q: What does the repeated absence of a helper emphasize?

answers: Both picture crushing and staining, with the enemies compared to grapes
Both describe a journey through the wilderness
challenge.explanation: The winepress image represents the crushing of the nations and the staining of the garments.
challenge.q: What connection is made between treading the winepress and divine vengeance?

answers: Redemption is delayed until after vengeance
Both are presented as having arrived at the appointed time
challenge.explanation: The verse says, “the day of vengeance is in mine heart, and the year of my redeemed is come.”
challenge.q: How are vengeance and redemption related in verse 4?

paragraphs.title: God’s Kindness and Guidance in the Past

easy.explanation: The prophet says, “I will mention the lovingkindnesses of the Lord.”
easy.q: What does the prophet mention at the beginning of the passage?

easy.explanation: The Lord said, “Surely they are my people, children that will not lie.”
easy.q: How did the Lord regard Israel?

easy.explanation: The passage recalls Moses and the people whom God brought up out of the sea.
easy.q: Who is named as leading the people through the sea?

medium.explanation: The passage says that God saved, redeemed, bore, and carried them.
medium.q: What did the Lord do for Israel in their affliction?

answers: The Lord became their enemy and fought against them
The Lord immediately led them through the sea
medium.explanation: The text says, “therefore he was turned to be their enemy, and he fought against them.”
medium.q: What happened after Israel rebelled and vexed God’s holy Spirit?

answers: You guided and directed your people
medium.explanation: The passage describes God guiding Israel through the deep and the wilderness.
medium.q: What does “thou lead thy people” mean in this context?

answers: God led them safely so that they would not stumble
The people remained in one place
challenge.explanation: The passage says God led them through the deep “that they should not stumble.”
challenge.q: What quality of God’s guidance is shown in the description of the wilderness?

answers: Past deliverance is presented as an example of continuing mercy and guidance
God’s kindness ended before Moses’ day
Moses acted without any connection to God
challenge.explanation: The prophet recalls God’s mercy, salvation, and guidance of Israel through Moses.
challenge.q: How does the passage connect God’s kindness with his leadership in Moses’ day?

answers: God saves Israel, yet Israel rebels against him
Israel is always faithful and God never acts
God and Israel have no relationship
challenge.explanation: The passage presents both God’s compassion and Israel’s rebellion against his holy Spirit.
challenge.q: What central tension appears in the relationship between God and Israel?

paragraphs.title: Israel’s Prayer for the Return of Mercy and Redemption

answers: To the kings of the nations
easy.explanation: The prophet says, “Look down from heaven, and behold,” addressing the Lord.
easy.q: To whom does the prophet direct his request?

answers: The king of the nations only
easy.explanation: The prophet declares, “thou, O Lord, art our father, our redeemer.”
easy.q: How does the prophet call the Lord?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “our adversaries have trodden down thy sanctuary.”
easy.q: What is described as having been trodden down?

medium.explanation: The prophet asks, “where is thy zeal and thy strength” and speaks of God’s mercies.
medium.q: What does the prophet ask God to reveal again?

answers: That God return and act for his people
That the people leave their land
That the enemies return to the sanctuary
medium.explanation: The request asks God to return to his servants and act for the tribes of his inheritance.
medium.q: What is requested by the words “Return for thy servants’ sake”?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the holy and glorious dwelling place of God.
medium.q: What does “the habitation of thy holiness and of thy glory” mean?

answers: To emphasize that the Lord himself is their Father and Redeemer
To erase the memory of the patriarchs
To say that the people did not belong to Israel
challenge.explanation: The contrast highlights the people’s direct relationship with God as their Father and Redeemer.
challenge.q: Why does the prophet say that Abraham was ignorant of them and Israel did not acknowledge them?

answers: They are in a humiliated and ruined condition
They are at the height of their power
They rule over all nations again
challenge.explanation: The people possess the land only briefly while their adversaries tread down the sanctuary.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the description of the people in the hands of their adversaries?

answers: It expresses longing for God’s visible and powerful intervention
It expresses a desire to flee from God
It describes Israel’s departure from Egypt
challenge.explanation: The appeal for God to look down and return expresses a longing for divine mercy and intervention.
challenge.q: How does the ending connect with the desire for God to act from heaven?
